Check parameter and latent-state identifiability diagnostics

check_latent_identifiability.Rd

Evaluates simulation- or plug-in-based diagnostics for the CDCM identifiability assumptions involving the effective connectivity matrices and the latent neural states.

Usage

check_latent_identifiability(
  A,
  B,
  u,
  z,
  block_indices = NULL,
  tol = 1e-08,
  warn = TRUE
)

Arguments

A

A \(d \times d\) numeric matrix giving the baseline effective connectivity matrix.

B

A list of \(d \times d\) numeric matrices giving the modulatory connectivity matrices. The length of B should match the number of stimulus inputs.

u

A \(T \times m\) numeric matrix encoding the stimulus inputs at each observation time.

z

A \(T \times d\) numeric matrix of latent neural states evaluated at the observation times. Rows correspond to time points and columns correspond to ROIs.

block_indices

Optional integer vector giving the block indices to check. If NULL, all eligible blocks with at least \(d + 1\) observations are checked.

tol

Numeric tolerance used for eigenvalue, rank, and determinant checks. Defaults to 1e-8.

warn

Logical; if TRUE, warnings are issued when diagnostics fail. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A list containing:

cond_A3

Logical indicating whether A3 is satisfied for all checked blocks.

cond_A4

Logical indicating whether A4 is satisfied for all checked blocks.

all_ok

Logical indicating whether both diagnostics are satisfied.

block_results

A data frame containing block-level diagnostic results.

Details

This function checks the CDCM assumptions involving the true parameters and latent discrete observations. Unlike the design assumptions, these conditions generally cannot be verified directly from real data because the true parameters and latent states are unknown. Therefore, this function is intended primarily for simulation studies, where A, B, and z are known, or as a post-fit plug-in diagnostic using posterior summaries.

For each checked block \(b\), the function forms $$ \tilde A^{(b)} = A + \sum_{i = 1}^m \tilde u_i^{(b)} B_i, $$ where \(\tilde u^{(b)}\) is the block-level stimulus vector, obtained from the first row of u within block \(b\). Assumption A3 is checked by verifying that \(\tilde A^{(b)}\) has real and distinct eigenvalues.

Assumption A4 is checked by constructing $$ X^{(b)} = [x_0^{(b)}, \ldots, x_d^{(b)}], \qquad x_j^{(b)} = [z(t^{(b)} + t_j)^T, 1]^T, $$ from the first \(d + 1\) latent observations in block \(b\), and checking whether \(X^{(b)}\) has full rank.

When used with posterior means from real data, these checks should be interpreted only as plug-in diagnostics conditional on the quality and convergence of the posterior fit.
